I was always afraid to try soulseborne games as I don't have enough time to spend hours and hours a day on a single game. The first 10 hours of Sekiro made me feel like this game is going to take forever to finish. I was having fun, but I felt like I could have bought some other game that I would have enjoyed much more, rather than buying this game where I am stuck in a single place for hours and hours. However, there comes a point where the combat just clicks. A sort of turning point. Once that happens, there is no going back. Sekiro is my most favourite game ever and I recommend everyone to try it atleast once in their life. From being stuck on Gybou Oniwa for day to defeating the owl and corrupted monk within the same day, I really came a long way hahaha.

Do you remember the game Tenchu? This reminds me of that, except it's on insane difficulty. I have died too many times to count. You''ll think you might be good at games until you fire this one up. The fighting is exceptionally hard and you need to be perfect at it. The graphics are great and the story is awesome. I can't complain how hard it is because it's obvious that it's how they meant it to be. That being said, I am not the Shinobi........I can hardly kill a basic trash mob and have skipped many little mini bosses because I get my bum handed to me. If you want to play a game where you die A LOT........this is for you. If you have anger issues.....tread carefully.

It's just amazing, loved the bosses and all the endings. The combat was quite iffy at first but after getting used to it, it felt pretty good; The story is definitely my favorite part as compared to dark souls it's more in-your-face and you don't have to watch videos to understand what's going on.

I’ve played the Dark Souls trilogy, but this game clicked in a way the others did not. the art is beautiful and the combat has a great flow to it
I fully believe this game has one of if not the best and most fluid sword play of any game I've ever played, we can only wish to get more of this (even though it will never happen probably) :(
TOP 5 game for me, im on ng+++++. if your looking for a game to challenge yourself and that has great combat i suggest you get Sekiro , stop looking at reviews and buy it now xD.

Starscream's Review of Sekiro Shadows Die Twice

Sekiro is so F$$$$$$ sick. Seriously, it's like wielding a Decepticon energon blade while slicing through Autobots. The parry system is hands down the best I've ever experienced in a game, and I've been around longer than Optimus Prime himself. You actually feel like a ninja with every precise, well-timed block and riposte. And those ruthless kills? They're some of the most satisfying moments in gaming, like blasting Metroplex right in his kisser.

The game's setting and atmosphere are absolutely stunning, as if Megatron himself crafted it with his own hands. From the eerie forests to the sprawling castles, everything is meticulously designed to immerse you in a world of ancient Japanese folklore. The sound design is top-notch too, with every sword slash and enemy grunt adding to the game's already intense ambiance. It's like you're right in the middle of a battle with those pesky Autobots.

It's not an easy game, but once you get the hang of it, Sekiro becomes an absolute blast to play. It's definitely not for those weak-willed, squishy humans, but if you're up for a challenge and want to feel like a total badass while doing it, Sekiro is a must-play for any Decepticon. I give it a solid 10/10, or should I say, a Starscream/10.

This game is brutal, and so enjoyable to play. Another great piece of work from FromSoftware.

It's difficult to master the bosses, but it feels so gratifying when you do so.

I can't recommend this high enough.

~David.

I straight up hate Soulsborne genre games. The tediously long trips after every frequent death make those games a chore to play.

Not the case with Sekiro. Checkpoints are frequent and well placed, doing away with some of the frustration that typically comes with these sorts of games.

Sekiro is fun as hell, bringing old memories of Tenchu games along with Akira Kurosawa films. The cathartic sprays of blood every time you defeat an enemy are addicting, and the traversal mechanics make you feel like ninja Spiderman.

I’m in love.

Difficult. Satisfying. Went in expecting a sequel to Tenchu, and it kinda didn't satisfy that hunger for me. But I got like half a Tenchu mixed with part Shadow of the Colossus and part Dark Souls boss fights but with less dodge roll spam and more parries. Really enjoyed my first playthrough and I can't stop thinking about it. 10/10.

Finally got to see what the hype was about. Elden Ring being my first Fromsoft title on PS5, this is an amazing game, can see why it got game of the year honestly. Your gonna need patience when learning, but don't hesitate play smart, aggressive and be ready for anything thrown at you. Got all the achievements at 100hrs. Plan to go back for the boss rush as well while I know all bosses pretty well now.

It is a truly great game, with a great challenge, not for complainers. The difficulty is of another level, not suitable for craps, but once you master the techniques you will not be able to stop playing it, it is great and very replayable. I finished it 4 times completely to take the 4 different paths and corresponding endings that it has. I fully recommend it.

Unlike the (relatively) generous dodge-rolling encouraged in most other soulsborne games, this game forces you to engage with the attacks of enemies with precise parrying. As a result the gameplay almost feels like a rhythym game, pulling you into the tempo of every enemy's attacks. This is especially true for bosses, and the mastery you're forced to develop makes every victory feel so much more satisfying.

Sekiro is my favorite souls game. I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys soulsborne games.

Good game with amazing bossfights and mediocre replay value. One of not many games that are worth buying in modern times, where most games are too easy and made for casual scrubs, rather than people who can dedicate few hours a day learning games. Got platinum trophy + I beat Owl charmless, but then I decided to speed up my platinum run rather than mastering true monk fight while charmless.

Mods that make game harder are additional benefit that add some more longevity to the game.

sekiro grabbed me by the neck and put me in a chokehold for like 2 months where all i did was play this game. i have never played any other game where the combat is as satisfying as sekiro's. each area of the game is beautiful and the main characters are extremely likeable and yes i cried during the purification ending. 100/10 i dont think i will ever stop playing sekiro

Sekiro is what I consider to be Fromsoft's magnum opus.
A game that requires you to rely only on yourself and is built meticulously around it.
The barrier of entry is low, but the ceiling for mastery is high.
This game starts as a puddle but ends as an ocean,
comparable only to games like Devil May Cry.
The player expression is here, so express yourself and remember wolf, that hesitation is defeat.

If one were to amalgamate Onimusha, Ninja Gaiden, God of War and the very essence of the Dark Souls series into a single entity you would get a masterfully crafted work of art that is Sekiro. Every other 3rd person action/rpg game will perpetually be compared to Sekiro's fluid combat so be warned.

After 100%ing it, I can say this game is truly an undeniable challenge that will test your patience and character.

The story is beautiful and paced well alongside the bosses and obstacles you face on your journey. The characters are unique and fit the world-building perfectly.

The Wolf is an honorable man, and will go to the furthest lengths imaginable to fulfill his duty,
this mirrors the sheer mental lengths you will go to in order to finish this game, especially if you want to complete all the achievements, speaking from experience.

The combat is arguably the best from FromSoftware.
It feels grounded, responsive, and weighted thanks to the unique parrying system.
It feels like you're actually fighting the boss, instead of rolling around like a maniac and stabbing them in between hits.
You're a formidable foe in this game. Staying aggressive and attacking ruthlessly is a key part of winning and 'getting good', which is not the advice I'd give for other Soulslike games.

Every player familiar with Soulslike games knows that feeling of finally figuring out a boss, and this game gives the most satisfying version of it out of any of them

For people wishing to test themselves and like the idea of a head-on approach to combat where you can stand unmoving, look the boss dead in the eyes and say "I see it. I know how to beat you."
If that all sounds good, then this is the game for you.

This was my first Fromsoft game. 

Got it at launch on Xbox, Hated it. Put it down for a year. Then, during the pandemic, I decided "why not give this another go?" Proceeded to immeadiately 100% it. Its frustrating, in fact, down right infuriating at points. But in my opinion, its a masterpiece. 

Loved it so much I got it again on PC, and intend fully to 100% it again.

Easily one of my favorite games of all time. It demands a specific type of playstyle, which you'll need to learn if you want to have a good time, unlike in Dark Souls. However, I think that specific playstyle is so gratifying once it clicks that it's 100% worth it. The world, characters, and story are all amazing if you pay attention and play through multiple times for the little details.

Honestly, it's up there with Majora's Mask and Outer Wilds for me.

Don't let my small amount of time in this game fool you. I definitely enjoy this game. I literally have recorded this game every time I play it. I then watch the video before I play it the next time to see what mistakes I made to help me. This game has me using my brain and exercising ways around issues and problems. I love the game and enjoy it every time I play. I never thought I would see mods for this but there is some mostly cosmetic but there is a difficulty mod (harder difficulty then default). If your a fan of darksouls, bloodborne, etc. this game follows that style from "From Software". At this point in my play-through I definitely Recommend it and have enjoyed it even when I yelled from fustration.

your experience with Sekiro will go like this :

- Install the game
- Die Again and Again
- Get frustrated and Angry
- Uninstall.
- Reinstall later, thinking “maybe this time…will be different”

Sekiro enemy/boss music is officially my alarm sound after the experience.
Shinobi stuff man how can you not like this. Plus we have swords, monkeys, ghosts, awesome scenic views, an edgylord (yes genichiro i'm sorry i still like you) obsessed with power and bad memory by drinking all that sake.

Sekiro have one of the most satisfying combat system. With focus on deflecting and parrying incoming attacks in order to break the opponent. Reading the moves and figuring out how to counter the moves feels incredibly rewarding. Combining this system with a incredibly immersive world just like the souls games that came before this.

If you love rewarding combat and immersive worlds then this is the game for you. Even if you haven't played any other fromsoft games you can start with this one. It is also a easier game to get into than the souls games.

A much less accessible, yet equally fun Souls-Like game.

Wouldn't recommend it for your first rodeo, but if you've played a Souls-Like and are craving more, Sekiro is what you're after.

Genuinely extremely difficult, there's no cheesing some of the brick-wall bosses here.

A pretty good game if you like rpgs with complex, timed combat. Sekiro has a decent "talent tree" system that allows you to learn new abilities and upgrade passives. If you like darksouls this is yet another success by Fromsoft. Very unique blend of "stealth", assassinations, and head on combat. 10/10

Another very well-made FromSoft Game and a well deserved Game of the Year. If it would not be for Bloodborne, i would say it's their best so far, in my eyes (with DS1 and DS3 not far behind those two). It certainly is the most beautiful of them, with one of the most beautiful boss fights in gaming history.

They managed to make a totally new combat system for Sekiro. It's so different from former games, but it's on point and actually the best thing about the game. You can and have to jump, dodge, deflect, sprint, use items, skills and your tools in so many different ways, it's just never stops to get boring.

You have to study your enemies, Mini-Bosses and Bosses until you know all the mechanics by heart and get the right countermeasures for all there attacks. And the felling for beating each Boss (also the Mini-Bosses) the first time is so incredibly rewarding. You will have a smile on your face the whole day long. Ok, at least until the next boss fight. With each one of them (well most) is pretty unique and very memorable.

Story, Lore, NPCs and Atmosphere is typical FromSoft. Deep, dark, melancholic and absolutely gorgeous. An amazing soundtrack and a wonderful game-world just completes the whole experience.

If you like the genre and still thinking about it, don't think twice and just give them your money. It's worth every penny.
My girlfriend beat all the bosses and minibosses in this game without getting hit one single time. The game's cool, but she is cooler.

Once you learn to use Katana for attacking, you will need to learn how to use it to defend yourself. Only at this point game will start to be cool. Before that you will suffer. But pain is needed in order to embrace focus, and become the REAL SHINOBI.

Originally refunded this game because of its difficulty but decided to give it another shot and I am so glad that I did. It has extremely good combat, incredible world design, beautiful art direction, and a great story. While the combat can seem very punishing at first, if you start to finally get the hang of it (and have the "click" moment that many people talk about; happened to me at the top of Ashina Castle) you will have once of the most rewarding experiences in all of gaming. That being said, I don't think it's for everyone and it isn't without its flaws in some areas, but it still is absolutely worth giving a shot nevertheless if you're into this genre.
Definitely the most difficult game I have ever played, but also a contender for my favorite game of all time.
no joke the best game i ever played maybe only elden ring can keep up with it pretty hard at first but you will learn to flow of the game pretty quickly and has some of the best bosses ever

I've watched a lot of streamers and youtubers play souls-like games — Sekiro, Bloodborne, Elden Ring — and I always thought it looked fun. I knew these games were hard, but I had no idea how hard until I experienced it myself. Being 100% honest, I overestimated myself: I really thought I could handle it. I even considered requesting a refund before the 2-hour limit, but I decided to keep trying. Almost 7 hours in, it still hasn't clicked for me. I think this genre just isn't for me. I'm removing Elden Ring from my wishlist and forgetting about Bloodborne. I bought this on the summer sale, and I'm honestly upset I picked it over other games. But at least I got to experience a souls-like firsthand and reached my own conclusion: it's not for me.

This game is amazing - like all Soulsborne games there's a learning curve and I can see why some who like the other games (Dark Souls in particular) have mixed feelings on this one. That being said - i love it. The lack of shield forces you to be aggressive (and that's really the key to playing the game successfully) although a block move does exist and later on you can get a funky Japanese Umbrella made of steel that you can use as a shield....what's not to love there right!?!
I very much like the level design, I've not enjoyed exploring a Souls game as much as this one since the first DS to be honest.
The boss fights are as frustrating as ever - as are the mini bosses (which I've often had greater difficulty with).
Once i finish this game (if i can!) I'll try to update this review - i got this in a sale for about £25....to me that is a bargain for the hours that I've got out of it so far as i'm only about a third to half way through the game at 32 hours in.

I consider Sekiro a brilliant masterpiece that delivers incredibly tight and gratifying combat wrapped in a gripping atmosphere with beautiful style. The pure satisfaction of mastering its challenges - which are genuinely hard but never unfair - is second to none.

Even after multiple playthroughs, it still easily stands as one of my all-time favorites.
Ended up being a little too difficult for me but gosh was it rewarding when I'd finally defeat an enemy!

I'm not very good at From Software's games, but I enjoy how they combine rigour and freedom. You need to learn how to play these in order to succeed, and that won't be for everyone. It's not all I want from games, but I've found that every couple of years I greatly enjoy the process of learning the ropes, getting better and making it to the end. And Sekiro is also wonderfully rich in environments, characters and enemies - even if it's the From Software game that takes the most rethinking if you're used to the Dark Souls template and is therefore more likely to put some of the developers' fans off.

This is honestly one of the best games I have ever played. One of the few games where I actually wanted to get all the achievements. I had loads of fun fighting bosses even If I did die all the time but I seriously recommend this game even If it is very hard. I also think it's better than Elden Ring.

When I was a child. One day I went to the video game store to buy Metroid 2.
And then the sales lady told me "It may be too difficult for you."
But I said "It's ok! I want this!"

Some months later. After having finished the game, I went to the video game store to tell that to the lady.
But I found the store gone.

Sekiro reminded me of the story and the days I wasn't afraid of challenges.

This was my first FromSoftware game and I absolutely loved it! I really enjoyed the rhythm based combat and found it very satisfying once I mastered it. There is really nothing bad I can say about the game, except for maybe that it's a bit short. I know that some didn't like the lack of weapon variety, but I honestly didn't mind it. Mastering only one weapon while having the prosthetic arm tool to help you a bit was perfect for me as a newcomer. My favorite thing about Sekiro is probably the atmosphere. The music and environments are just on point and I wish I could spend more time in this world. I really hope the success of this game means we will see a sequel sometime in the future. Definitely recommend it!

I write this review after 64 hours, 4 full playthroughs, and a 100% of this game to tell you that it is indeed the best FromSoftware game that is not named Bloodborne or Armored Core. This game is the definition of Aura Farming and nothing less. If you feel uncool while playing this game, I've got some bad news for you. The swordplay is satisfying in a visual and audial that you just don't get from other titles in the FromSoftware franchise. In summation, Aura Farm shinobi go *shing* wit da sword. Very nice. 4.8/5

Just play ittttt

Best combat system ever (for action rpg games at least).

Best final boss ever.

I'd take a Sekiro 2 over any bloodborne, dark souls or elden ring sequel.
Peak combat across all soulslike games. It's not even as difficult as other Fromsoft titles once you get past the steep learning curve.

I'm late to the party on this game, but I love it. It is a pain in the ass at times, but learning the ins and outs of the game is very satisfying. It is a FromSoft game that doesn't play like a Souls title which is a unique thing to see from FromSoft. The settings and level design are breathtaking. The bosses are difficult but satisfying to finally get the better of. I must say I am a huge fan of the newer system of fighting with a huge emphasis on parrying and being aggressive and I find each individual fight very fulfilling. I can definitely recommend this game, even to people that aren't fans of the Souls series as I find that it stands on its own very well and is a unique experience. I'm over halfway through the game on my first run and intend to come back once I've finished it. In closing, buy this game if you are interested, it will be a challenging time, but is a breathtaking experience all around.

Hesitation is defeat.

A great game to progress through, and it gets more fun with more playthroughs.

It feels like FromSoftware and Souls games peaked here. The combat system, the movement, the level design, and the bosses are all standards by which I judge these types of games. This one game is usually the best of all categories. I wish more of this game's play style and boss design made it into future titles.

i enjoyed this game a lot the bossfights are insanely good and the parrying system makes it so unique
the sound of parrying is so relaxing and when an enemy hit a combo and you can deflect it perfectly and counter attack is so PEAK
there is a boss i didnt like but im not gonna spoiler anything
i bought this on a sale not the full price
i do reccomend purchasing this game it makes so good of a time consuming activity

Doubt that I can ever find a game like this ever again, 10/10. Never had so much fun in a long time!
I finished the with while having the demon bell effect on all time! I was forged in the flames of Sekiro!
this game is very good and very enjoyable. is just the bosses are very hard and could be hard for begginers
